content.text: This is necessary for a clean solution to FCREPO-696. Maybe it's worth considering to increase the priority of this issue.
This was the utility class I was thinking of during the call:
could be used for managing uploaded files (but might need some work to ensure uploaded files are not removed between requests) and
could be used for managing temp files.

Further note on this - using File.delete() is not always removing files (this can be due eg to a stream using the file left open but doesn't seem to be the case in my testing) - I've seen multiple forum posts on this; will be interesting to see if the Apache Commons purger manages to get around this; maybe a test case to check that the upload/temp directories get cleaned up properly.
Worth noting FCREPO-766, particularly that IOUtils.copy() (and other methods) do not close streams, this could be the cause of temp files failing to be deleted (especially on Windows it seems)

Code for managing temp and uploaded files is somewhat distributed through the codebase, it would be better to have this in a single unit of code - a temp file management class (with an interface) to manage creating, reading and cleaning up temporary files.
DefaultManagement - creates and reads uploaded files, including time-based expiry of these files
DatastreamManagedContent - creates and reads uploaded files through DefaultManagement (thus requires authorization for the API-M methods)
FOXMLDODeserializer creates temp files (for inline binary managed content) (and other Deserializers)
DefaultDOManager deletes temp files (managed inline binary content)
